note: Selected artwork and review status follow the catalogue. Original paintings and editable prompts remain in the asset library. This manifest is build-time provenance, never a page request.

review.notes: Broad pale barrier arch and exterior impact remain distinct at 32px in color and grayscale. Two sheltered figures are clearer at 48/64px; the barrier stays the primary small-size cue.
Lifted oval plate, exposed spring and two outward ground ridges remain legible at 32px. The warm light conveys physical upheaval rather than a fire spell.

Ash-grey heart mass, branching vessels and diagonal chain separate at 32px; orange fissures strengthen the color version. Grayscale retains the bound-heart silhouette, while small ash flakes are larger-size detail.
Bright diagonal dagger and rear shoulder remain separate at 32px and in grayscale. Close rear contact clearly supports the source positional strike; blood stays a small secondary accent.
Bow arms, forward bolt and squat pedestal are readable at 32px. The pale straight firing trace and dark gaps distinguish a planted ranged device.
Tall pole and two broad folded sections of torn cloth are clear at 32px, including grayscale. The low rally ripple remains subordinate to the standard.
Lavender inward spiral and uneasy head profile remain visible at 32px. The full painting shows the whisper entering the ear; this fine detail is secondary at small size.

Pale mask, long ears, curled tail and binding sweep remain visible at 32px in color and grayscale. The painting follows the inspected local familiar's main features; crystal satellites are clearer at 48/64px.
Wide chalice bowl, narrow stem and foot remain readable at 32px. Red liquid and suspended drop strengthen the life-reservoir metaphor; padlock detail is chiefly visible at larger sizes.
Separated metal quills form a clear radiating silhouette above the shoulder at 32px, including grayscale. The small reflected-impact spark remains secondary.
Bright curved blade and two opposing broad cut trails remain separate at 32px. The small buckler is subordinate and does not turn the defined double cut into a shield bash.
Foreground caltrop's raised point and three grounded prongs remain distinguishable at 32px. Two smaller caltrops establish the field at larger sizes without overwhelming the main silhouette.

Revised r02 adds broad lit red fabric planes. The upper sweep and lower return fold now remain distinguishable at 32px grayscale, preserving the empty center and ghostly decoy. Earlier low-contrast r01 is retained.
Reviewed original and reduced sizes. Warm swept wings and light barred breast retain the hunting falcon silhouette at 32 pixels; the glove is secondary. Uses the accepted hunting falcon reference.

review.notes: The broad hook and diagonal chain remain visible at 32 pixels and in grayscale. The hooked armor establishes a pull rather than an unanchored chain projectile.
Frontal open mouth, raised shield and incoming weapons distinguish the taunt from the earlier side-profile War Cry. The mouth and shield rim remain the strongest small-size landmarks.

Selected r02 after the first version blended helmet, shoulder and dust at 32 pixels. Broad steel highlights now separate the lowered head and leading shoulder; dust stays secondary. Original r01 and derivatives are retained.
Bright contact between the hands and bandaged arm reads at 32 pixels. Dark curling curse fragments separate from the healing light; finer anatomy is legible in the larger exports.

review.notes: Large empty hood, pale rim and folded cloth remain readable at 32px in color and grayscale. Low-contrast outer smoke supports concealment without competing with the hood.
The single forward boot and pale mist edge remain recognizable at 32 pixels in color and grayscale. The trailing decoy is subordinate and clearer in the larger exports.

The tilted lyre and pale outward ring remain recognizable at 32 pixels and in grayscale. Fine strings read more clearly at 48/64, while the instrument frame and finishing shockwave carry the small icon.
Large pointing hand and three converging gold paths remain distinct at 32 pixels. Individual minion details are secondary and clearer at larger sizes; the command converges on one target.
The illuminated ground ellipse, low fire rim and planted armored foot survive all reviewed sizes and grayscale. Its grounded circle differs from the raised Aegis Ward dome.

Selected r02 after r01 lost the running pose in 32px grayscale. Stronger light across hood, shoulder, raised thigh and leading shin separates the angular running silhouette from the dark background. Earlier original and derivatives preserved.
Broad forward blade and silver slash wake remain clear at 32 pixels and in grayscale. The compact fighter behind the blade distinguishes this damaging lunge from plain Dash.

The upright luminous lure and raised beckoning hand dominate at 32 pixels. Spear penetration and smaller escaping rogue are clearer at larger sizes. Its human silhouette differs from Summon Phantasm's limb-free cowl.

Pale bowed face and four separated violet ward fragments remain visible at 32 pixels and in grayscale. The quiet downward expression and broken shell distinguish this curse from shouted or charm effects.
The unequal bronze fork and its deep central gap give a clear silhouette at every size. Jagged violet sound ribbons remain secondary to the fork and survive grayscale.

The broad raised stone slab and lower initial hammer impact form separate masses at 32 pixels. Large fissures and ochre dust convey physical upheaval; the image has one origin rather than Aftershocks' multiple centers.

The bright incoming violet seed and gray decaying armor separate at 32 pixels; finer peeling leather and lingering tendrils are clearer at 48/64. Grayscale retains the strike point and opposing armor diagonal.
The large hooked blade and dark old tear remain readable at 32 pixels and in grayscale. The small crimson concentration at the tip is secondary; no exposed tissue is shown.

The bounded pale segment stands out against the dim crimson vitality ribbon at 32 pixels and in grayscale. The dark armor behind it stays subordinate. This is a metaphor for the source's life window, not an anatomical target marker.

Three returning shafts, a broad foreground spearhead and an open receiving gauntlet form clear diagonals at 32px. The precise withdrawal from armor is clearer at 48/64; the return is physical steel, not a chain.
Exactly five separate knives were verified in the original. Their spaced pale blades retain the fan silhouette at 32px and in grayscale; the launching hand stays secondary.

review.notes: The continuous open crescent and black hollow remain unmistakable at 32px and in grayscale. Its trailing mist and low stone path suggest forward travel rather than a stationary circle.
The pale stone at the helmet and turned head remain readable at 32px; the eye and throwing-hand details are clearer at larger sizes. The composition isolates one provoked foe.
Pass at 32/48/64px and 32px grayscale: the bright block head and open spiral remain distinct; the secondary casting hand is clearer at 48/64. The hammer is airborne, not held.

Pass at all reviewed sizes: pale screaming face and ragged expanding fan stay recognizable in grayscale. Recoiling targets are secondary detail most legible at 48/64; no literal cold-damage crystals are introduced.
Pass at all reviewed sizes: the linen-wrapped fist, bent forearm and curved hook remain distinct from weapon strikes. The helmet is secondary at 32; no anatomy defect or blood detail observed.
Pass at all reviewed sizes: broad silver mace fins and dark grooves make a heavy diagonal silhouette; compact impact and helmet separate at 48/64. One blow, with no repeat-attack ghosts.
Pass at all reviewed sizes: a bright continuous shallow whipping curve remains visible even in 32px grayscale. The handle and cropped grip are secondary; the large dark hollow prevents flame clutter.

Pass at all reviewed sizes: three separated olive shell masses, pale ridges and a prominent front body read as a swarm. The foreground pointed keel, pincer jaws and angular legs follow the current Swarmling reference; finer rear anatomy is occluded and not claimed as a model validation.

Pass at all reviewed sizes: the bright blade emerges coherently from the dark scabbard mouth, with two distinct hands and a clean slash wake. Draw-focused crop differs from Dash Strike's running attacker; collar glint is clearest at 48/64.

Pass at all reviewed sizes: a continuous rounded ice shell encloses a calm defender. The large circular protective silhouette differs from Flash Freeze's jagged target block. Fine basal fractures and palms resolve better at 48/64.
Pass at all reviewed sizes: one dark armored target is continuously wreathed in upward fire, with no incoming bolt or beam. The bright chest kindle and helmet silhouette survive grayscale.

R02 passes all reviewed sizes: paired matching helmets and crossed blades remain separate in 32px grayscale; a broader whisper ribbon links the visors. R01 original, derivatives and first sheet are preserved.

Pass at all reviewed sizes: one continuous straight hot core links the casting hand to the target edge. Distinct from fireballs, Flame Arrow and Hellfire Lash. Small hand anatomy and target details resolve better at 48/64.

R02 passes all reviewed sizes: stronger head, shoulder and hand contours identify a vanishing figure while the torso remains transparent. The wall continuing through the body is clearest at 48/64 and original size. Intentionally quieter than offensive icons; distinct from Cloak's opaque hood. R01 is preserved.

Ordered ember, ice, lightning and lavender force tokens lead into one casting palm. The palm and descending weave remain distinct at 32/48/64px and 32px grayscale; individual token order is clearest in the original. This is one illustrative sequence, not a claim that four particular runes are required.
Calm closed-eye profile and pursed lips release smooth broad air folds. Face, robe and expanding breath survive 32px color and grayscale, distinct from Harrowing Wail's anguished mouth.

A single linen-wrapped wrist drives an open palm into a training plate. The pale diagonal forearm and upright hand remain legible at all three reduced sizes and grayscale; faint practice impressions are supporting detail rather than a visible stack counter.

Tall flat-topped wooden tower shield, separated advancing boots and a rear dust wake distinguish this from Shield Up's planted kite shield. The long shield plane remains readable at 32px color/grayscale; walking anatomy is clearer at 48/64px.

Frontal open palm, supporting darker hand and localized healing light read at all reviewed sizes. The tiny closing scratch is clearest in the original; the broad palms and central glow carry the small icon. No cleansing tendrils or armor repair.

One upright arrival breaks into amber refractive strips across a dark gap, with an incomplete departure contour. The bright shoulder/cloak edge survives 32px color/grayscale; no second solid character, enemy or attack. Distinct from Shadow Step's attack and Cloudstep's moving boot.

Leading wrapped fist and separate waiting fist form a clear pair of straight diagonal arms, unlike Haymaker's single hook. Both fists remain readable at 32/48/64px and 32px grayscale. The faint earlier jab is supporting detail, not an additional solid hand or exact combo counter.

Heavy axe edge and shield rim meet at one gold contact flash. The broad axe blade, black gap and contact point survive all reviewed sizes and grayscale; the gold color supports the timing metaphor without a cast-bar diagram.

R02 lifts all three helmet and shoulder planes and enlarges the pale olive fletching. The receding rank is now distinct at 32px color/grayscale while the single horizontal arrow remains the brightest line. Earlier darker version and derivatives are preserved.

Vertical block-headed maul presses into a hunched armored shoulder. The square steel plane and bowed target remain distinct at all three reduced sizes and grayscale. Two small Fury embers are secondary larger-image detail, not required to identify the crushing blow.

Bright elliptical fire rim and three inward flame tongues retain a dark central gap at 32px color/grayscale. Clearly a closing ground ring rather than a lone fire column; the small central helmet is merely a scale cue and is clearer at larger sizes.

Downward leaf-shaped spearhead, upright shaft and small ground impact clearly show a planted weapon. The broad metal point and stone contact survive 32px grayscale; slack cloth and dissipating wake are secondary details. No target-pinning or pre-existing tripwire is implied.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. The short bright barb, red ribbon fork and turned helmet separate from Pinning Spear's ground-planted shaft. In 32px grayscale the shoulder/helmet and barb remain, while ribbon color is lost as expected.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Discrete teardrop heads and radial gaps remain obvious, including in 32px grayscale; central caster is secondary. It illustrates the projectile ring rather than promising an exact count at icon scale.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Two pale hoods sit inside a bright shared boundary with four outside elemental pressures. The hoods and dome survive 32px grayscale; individual element types rely more on color at that size. This represents resistance, not immunity.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Two separated boots, bright wraps and short ankle accents read as active footwork. Both boots remain distinct in 32px grayscale. No teleport or cloud is shown; the skill is a temporary speed/evasion buff.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. One softly planted shoe under a broad pale cloak hem creates a low, quiet silhouette distinct from Quickstep, Dash and Cloudstep. At 32px grayscale the hem, toe and ground contact remain; the fading heel is a secondary detail. Lowered detectability is not full invisibility.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. A single fleshy olive zombie rises from earth with pale head, reaching hand, ragged tunic and exposed ribs, following the inspected current adaptation. Head and hand remain in 32px grayscale; small ribs are secondary. Zombie is one of the equal-weight summon results, not a replacement for the skeleton option.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Broad pale wings and a tapering line of distinct flying bodies survive reduction and 32px grayscale; hook legs and eye details are secondary. Olive panelled shells, paired ivory eyes, two wings and hanging legs follow the inspected current Gnatling. The visible swarm is illustrative, not the cap of 24; flight direction is a composition choice.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Raised fist and leader above two allied heads distinguish the group blessing from lone War Cry and shield-led Challenging Shout. Golden breath crosses both allies. At 32px grayscale the fist and clustered head shapes remain; small facial details are secondary. Human and skeleton illustrate allies without limiting eligible recipients.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. A broad two-handed blade meets armor in one bright heavy impact; converging red Fury embers remain secondary. At 32px grayscale the blade and impact are strongest and the ember count is not legible, as expected. The charge illustration does not prescribe a fixed cost; skill can swing with none.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. One curved pale blade, a single torn leather seam and restrained dark-red blood accent clearly form a physical slash. Blade and tear survive 32px grayscale; bleed color and the two droplets are secondary. Weapon choice is illustrative and no excessive gore or repeated claw marks appear.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Broad war-pick/hammer sweep, damaged foreground armor and two recoiling helmets convey an answering arc with knockback. Hooked head and broad swing remain at 32px grayscale; the recent-hit dent is easier at 48/64px. Exact three-second damage gate and stun probability remain in metadata.

Original and 32/48/64px inspected. Exactly two crossed blades, a continuous guarded hand and a compact parry contact distinguish the close counter from Reprisal. Both diagonals and the foreground guard survive 32px grayscale. Static art represents the stance/counter without encoding its exact time window or multiplier.

Original shows one dominant violet chaos projectile hitting the hostile breastplate; a separate mint thread feeds the pale-hooded ally, not the caster. At 32px the projectile and separate ally light remain identifiable; the precise triple bond multiplier requires the description. Grayscale retains the diagonal projectile and lower ally highlight.

Original has a fixed inscribed floor circle and two planted feet beneath the robe. The broad cobalt ellipse and geometric center hold at 32/48/64px and in grayscale. No following halo or teleport trail. Abstract strokes are non-language; bonuses and duration remain in metadata.

Original clearly separates the foreground wielder wrist, pale allied hood receiving calm light, and burning enemy contact on the right. Axe and broad sweep read at 32px; ally healing is clearer at 48/64px and full size. Grayscale preserves the sweeping blade and separate upper hood. Representative melee weapon, no self-healing claim.

Original has exactly two matching hooded sword poses, with solid rear-left rogue and translucent violet forward-right mimic. Both hoods and directional blades remain separate at 32px; grayscale preserves the two head masses. Base one-clone state shown; later upgrades are not excluded. Smoke makes translucency clearer at larger sizes.
Pale purple hood and crescent-shaped arrival trail separate from the foreground armored back at 32px. The larger painting explicitly places the assassin behind the target.

Original shows cracked bronze bell with three elemental sectors: orange flame, blue-white ice and branching pale lightning. The dark bell mouth and luminous outer burst remain distinct at 32px and grayscale; elemental color helps separate sectors. Bell is a resonance metaphor, not equipment requirement; attunement details remain textual.

Original places the bright ice patch and abandoned boot impressions in the foreground, with the small solid mage at upper-right on bare stone. At 32px the dominant frost and separated arrival light survive; boot impressions and exact destination anatomy require larger sizes. Grayscale retains the dark gap between departure and arrival. No ice burst at destination.

Original shows one low charging knight behind a round shield with two cropped enemies displaced at the forward edge. Round boss, pale impact and backward dust survive 32/48/64px and grayscale. Compared with earlier Charge's shoulder-led movement; raised shield defines this identity. Small target anatomy is secondary; no guaranteed stun symbol.

review.notes: Original shows a broad translucent ivory-gray pressure sheet and two receding struck silhouettes, with no carrier or electricity. Flat leading edge stays clear at 32px and grayscale, while individual enemies read better at 48/64px. Physical bar projectile and knockback are represented; shown target count does not assert the maximum.

Original uses a pointing gauntlet, one intact highlighted hostile breastplate/helmet and two challenge ripples. Gold target and dark separating gap read at 32px; grayscale retains hand-to-target composition. Compared with Goad's thrown-stone hit and Expose Weakness's red gash; this has neither hit nor wound. Threat and health visibility remain textual.

Original shows one driving leaf spearhead and an older broken steel head retained in a nearby armor seam. Main diagonal point reads at all review sizes; retained fragment is clearest at 48/64px and original. Grayscale preserves metallic edges. No extracting shards, planted ribbon or ground pin. Exact impale share and later trigger remain in definition.

Original depicts a crouching sentinel behind one low broad curved guard with short steel spikes, no incoming strike and no release attack. Pale arch and spike row hold at 32px and grayscale, though the small helmet and hands need larger sizes. Wide held silhouette differs from Bulwark of Thorns' upright ivory-thorn contact scene and Shield Charge's round moving shield.

Original has one lobed yellow-green drifting cloud, edge spores, low haze and a cropped coughing hooded victim. Bright billows and dark valleys read at 32px and grayscale; individual spores and the victim are supporting larger-size cues. No instantaneous blast, projectile ring or new fungal actor. Exposure delay and poison chance are retained in metadata.

Original has one believable gloved hand, a pale four-card fan and a darker fifth card secretly held beneath it with a fine gold edge. Fan and glove silhouette remain clear at 32px and grayscale; concealed edge reads more strongly at 48/64px. No letters/numerals or thrown-card attack. Card count is a composition choice, not a mechanical quantity.

First original was too uniformly dark at 32px. Revision r02 adds broad natural sage-gray hood light, clearer face profile and taupe knee/boot planes, with deeper separating shadows and simpler reeds. Crouch, hood and folded knee now remain distinct at 32/48/64px and grayscale. Hunter stays opaque and patient, with no magical invisibility or speed trail. First original, derivatives and sheet preserved.

First original's small dark target was lost at 32px. Revision r02 enlarges helmet/torso/lifted knee and brightens broad worn-steel planes while keeping one tapered cyan needle, two interrupted temporal arcs and suspended fragments. Needle and arrested armored target now read at 32px and grayscale; full halted-pose details are clearer larger. A successful stasis outcome is shown, not a guaranteed lock; no ice or petrification. First version preserved.

Original separates a broad electrified falchion sweep against one cropped shoulder, three stored motes near the wrist and one thin discharge bolt reaching another enemy. Broad slash and separate upper bolt survive 32px and grayscale; precise mote count and timing are larger-size/textual details. Partial bank shown, not the full six-charge maximum or simultaneous discharge of all charges.

Original has exactly three adjacent gray-beige buttress slabs with beveled shoulders, wider feet, horizontal grooves and natural fractures. Three stepped tops and dark joints read at 32/48/64px and grayscale. Matches the inspected native construct's buttress/fracture cues without claiming a mapped 3D model. One three-segment placement is shown, not the total active maximum.

Original shows a living upper torso and bent arm with broad intact matte stone plates, warm skin still visible at neck and hand. Shoulder, folded arm and material boundary read at 32px and grayscale. Compared with Calcifying's struck forearm: no attacker, contact spark or damaging stone breakup here. Self-defense buff, not a frozen statue or full-body transformation requirement.

Original shows one thick vertical gold-white bolt into a single ground point, with a broad low impact ring and dark side gaps. Bolt and base read strongly at 32/48/64px and grayscale. Target marking is secondary; timing and shock chance require the description. No horizontal cast or persistent field is implied.

Original has a broad scuffed square maul pressing a two-handed guard downward over a bowed armored defender. Maul silhouette and compressed guard read at 32px and grayscale; knees and finer posture are clearer larger. Distinguished from Verdict's side follow-up and Piledriver's floor slam. Representative weapon, no guaranteed body destruction.

Original follows the inspected current Plains Wolf's long muzzle, sharp ears, pale cheek ruff, sand-gray natural coat and amber eye. Open hand and quiet sage bond strand remain separate at 32px; finger anatomy and detailed fur are larger-size cues. Grayscale keeps hand-to-muzzle gap. Representative eligible living beast, no claim that this one image depicts whistle/stance/revival or guarantees immediate taming.

Original shows a broad rounded-tip executioner's sword contacting intact armor while the off-balance foe's knee folds and shield lies down. Diagonal sword and two opposed bodies read at 32px and grayscale; prior broken-stance cues are clearest at 48/64px. No instant-kill or low-life threshold claim. Distinct from Sunder Maul's overhead guard-breaking composition.

Original shows exactly one pale lozenge-marked card with a bright physical edge, orange flame, pale-blue ice slivers and fine gold lightning together. Rectangular spinning card reads at 32px and grayscale; fine elemental traces are clearer at 48/64px. All damage components coexist; no random choice, lettering or card fan.

Revision r02 replaces arrow-shaped highlights with soft rim motion streaks on only the two smaller wheels. Held central wheel stays dark and stationary. Hand, large central wheel and separate smaller pair read at 32/48/64px and grayscale. Metaphor distinguishes other running cooldowns from untouched own cooldown; no exact reduction is asserted visually. First original, derivatives and sheet preserved.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Broad lateral iron hammer, long shaft and pale sweep remain recognizable at 32/48/64 and in 32px grayscale. The two recoiling armored figures and low masonry context are supporting details clearest at larger sizes. Strong horizontal swing differs from Sunder Maul's overhead blow and The Verdict's descending blade. No falling-masonry spell or required wall collision is implied by the saved semantics.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Single transparent dome, central dark arch and bright hourglass retain a clear silhouette at all reviewed sizes and in grayscale. Both arrows travel in the same direction without collision; differing wakes are readable in the original and larger preview, not relied upon at 32px. Painterly adaptation of the native arch/hourglass construct drawing, not a verified 3D model. Destructibility, duration, one-dome limit and precise enemy-projectile slow remain in the definition.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Low source orb, connecting ribbon and large raised shield stay separated by black gaps at all reviewed sizes and in grayscale. Cool source-to-guard transfer is visible, while an exact half-reserve measurement is intentionally not encoded. Shield shape is elongated by perspective rather than a strict round design; no source weapon subtype is required. Held-guard branch illustrated; standalone ward branch and stronger-pool behavior preserved in definition. No life expenditure or blood.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Large brass bell and broad gold directional compression fronts read at 32/48/64 and in grayscale, with electrical branches and backward-leaning enemies clearer at larger sizes. Directional wedge is distinct from circular nova or group chant imagery. Knockback and possible bewilderment remain correctly separate; no guaranteed status encoded.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Rounded mallet contacting intact breastplate, warm contact point and broad pale resonance contours survive all reviewed sizes and grayscale; target helmet and forearm resolve more clearly at 48/64. Image shows a physical strike with one illustrative cold-attuned outcome, not a promise of cold damage or simultaneous three-element effects. The representative mallet is not a required equipment type.

Original and contact sheet inspected. Single pointed diagonal liquid bolt, darker dense center and bright upper-right contact remain distinct at 32/48/64 and in grayscale. Three individual droplets and wet armor splash are clearest in larger previews. Narrow concentrated projectile is distinct from Poison Nova and Spore Bloom. Exact poison probability and stacking behavior remain in the definition.

Original and 32/48/64px plus 32px grayscale inspected. Raised conducting hand, central singer and following elliptical group ring read clearly; allied faces and the stored Verse pulse resolve better at larger sizes. Distinct from War Cry's profile shout and Coda's lyre. Amounts and Verse cap are definition data, not counted image marks.
Open mouth in side profile and two broad outgoing pressure arcs remain distinct at 32px, including grayscale. The face and armor keep it a martial rally.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Bright vertical fold and solid arrival silhouette remain separate at 32px and in grayscale; the dim departure trace and floor discontinuity are clearer at 48/64 and larger. The trace is a past position rather than a persistent clone. Exact delay cannot be read from a still and remains in the definition.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Wide planted legs, joined forearms and gold inner line retain a distinct grounded silhouette in color and grayscale. Blue reserve and upward conversion are clearer in color and larger sizes. No healing or life expenditure. The toggle, idling condition and mana floor remain in the definition.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Strong full ellipse of physical blade motion around the central warrior survives 32px grayscale; forward boot and two held blades resolve more fully at larger sizes. No wind funnel. Representative dual blades are not an added equipment requirement; channel duration and movement factor remain in definition.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Solid rapier and two fainter diverging motion wakes remain a readable directional fan at 32/48/64 and in grayscale, clearly distinct from Whirlwind's enclosing ellipse. Hilt details and advancing foot are secondary. Trails are successive bearings, not extra permanent weapons or a fixed count of simultaneous projectiles.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Bright poised curved blade and wrapped hands remain clear in grayscale and all sizes; three fading cadence wakes are clearest at 48/64. Crimson edge is supplementary and not required for silhouette recognition. Depicts the next-blow-ready state after cadence, not bleed applied by every third cut itself.

Original and 32/48/64px plus 32px grayscale inspected. Low circular pressure front, dark caster and large separated ice shards read at all sizes; intact armor beneath broken crusts is clearest at 48/64 and larger. Image shows consuming existing cold coatings, not growing a new ice prison or dismembering bodies. The condition and single damage multiplier remain in the definition.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Mouth-origin widening wet fan remains a clear yellow-green wedge in color and grayscale, with armor splashes and pitting clearer at larger sizes. Distinct from Venom Bolt's pointed projectile and Spore Bloom's cloud. No added creature identity or formula; source attack delivery and probabilistic poison/agony preserved.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Tall bright frontal shield, braced forward leg and sheltered group remain readable in grayscale and 32/48/64. Healing threads on a rear ally's arm and arrow contacts are clearest at larger sizes. Plain held shield is representative, not an equipment restriction. Frontal blocking and nearby ally mending are distinct from Aegis Ward's enclosing barrier and Transgression's mana transfer.

First review found weak grayscale torso contrast. r02 raises the armor value, separates the neck/arm and makes corrosion patches broader; the revised main armored silhouette and upper-left casting hand now remain clear at 32px and grayscale. Red haze indicates area curse without an explosive hit. First original, derivatives, sheet and revision prompt preserved. Exact armor/evasion reductions and seven-second duration remain in source data.

First original risked reading as airborne knockback because the running enemies lacked clear floor contact. r02 gives both a receding stone floor, planted stride and contact shadows. The low gold scent ring and crouched caster remain clear in all reductions/grayscale; fleeing backs and grounded feet are best seen at 64px and larger, not relied upon as fine 32px detail. Both originals and first derivatives/sheet preserved. Short panic is a status effect, not a physical throw.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Focused central magenta burst, large helmet/torso and smaller side responses remain distinct in grayscale and 32/48/64. Fraying curse ribbons and the pronouncing hand resolve more fully at larger sizes. Old bindings break rather than being newly applied; intact armor/body remains. Named eligible conditions and one consumption multiplier are recorded in the definition.

Original and 32/48/64px plus 32px grayscale inspected. Broad green bottle in a gloved hand retains a clear squat silhouette, distinct from existing red Life Flask and tall blue Mana Flask. Three breaking ailment threads are secondary details clearest at larger sizes. Cleansing and resistance are conveyed symbolically; the image does not encode charge count, exact ailment count or full immunity.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Dark singer against curling orange fire and jagged gold lightning remains recognizable in color and grayscale. Peripheral enemy reactions are illustrative, not a promise of a knockback effect. Direct damaging nova shown; the separate equipped two-song Responsory's ally mending is not falsely shown as every manual cast.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. Separated violet pointed missile heads along a sinuous guided route are distinct from the solid blue lance and large round release orbs at all reviewed sizes. The generated stream has six visible heads rather than the prompt's illustrative five; neither is a fixed gameplay volley count because this is a continuous channel. Fine electric branches are clearest at 48/64 and larger.

Original and all reviewed reductions inspected. One large diagonal lance and jagged blue lightning remain strong in grayscale and small reductions. The hand-side mana reservoir feeding the projectile is clearest at larger sizes; no exact percentage can be inferred from it. Distinct from Archon's Wellspring support's bowl and narrow emission. Single mana-fed lightning projectile, not a physical spear or ice.

First review found arrow shafts too distant at 32px. r02 brings four arrows and two separate low pair links close, brightens the shafts and removes unused foreground. Revised four-fletching/two-beam motif is clear at 32/48/64 and in grayscale.
